gaps.sentence: There weren't ___ chairs, so some guests had to stand.
gaps.explanation: 'Chairs' is countable and plural, so 'many' fits; 'much' and 'little' are for uncountables.
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so 'how much' is used.

gaps.sentence: She has two children. One lives in Leeds, and ___ lives in York.
gaps.hint: one of a pair of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... the other ...' is the pattern for exactly two; 'another' would imply more than two.

gaps.sentence: Three of the six books were mine; ___ were my sister's.
gaps.hint: the defined remainder of a set of six
gaps.explanation: 'The others' refers to the specific remaining books in the known set of six.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.
